Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexusShield Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexusShield Technologies' results for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Patel, Chief Financial Officer; and Chris Lopez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. NexusShield Technologies delivered a strong Q3, driven by continued demand for our cybersecurity solutions and our commitment to innovation. We are seeing increased adoption of our NexusShield One platform, which is helping organizations better protect themselves against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

Our focus remains on four key areas. First, accelerating zero trust and SASE adoption. Our push into Zero Trust Architecture, now integrated into our Secure Access Service Edge platform branded as NexusFlow, has transformed our offerings. In Q3, we added 247 net new enterprise customers, highlighted by a landmark $28 million ACV deal with a top-5 global bank that expanded from endpoint detection and response to full SASE convergence. This has propelled our Zero Trust ARR to $456 million, a 42% increase year-over-year and now 28% of total ARR, exceeding our 25% full-year goal. Technically, we've introduced generative AI-enhanced identity verification in NexusFlow, cutting lateral movement risks by 68% in beta trials according to MITRE Engenuity evaluations. Customer enthusiasm is clear, with an NPS of 72 for SASE, beating Zscaler's 68 based on recent 6sense data, and churn below 2% supported by 95% gross retention. For Q4, we aim for 30% year-over-year growth, backed by multi-year contracts averaging 4.2 years.

Second, advancing AI/ML-driven XDR and autonomous response. On top of our NexusShield XDR platform, we've ramped up investments in autonomous threat hunting, achieving 150% year-over-year growth in XDR module upsells and adding $112 million to RPO, which hit a record $2.1 billion, up 31% year-over-year. Our machine learning models, trained on 15 trillion daily signals, boast a 92% true positive rate with mean time to detect under 5 minutes, surpassing CrowdStrike's Falcon by 18% in G2 winter quadrant benchmarks. A major achievement is integration with our Cyber Fusion Center using NVIDIA GPUs for real-time behavioral analytics, neutralizing 4.2 million ransomware payloads in production with 75% auto-remediation. We've grown our managed detection and response service to 1,200 clients, up 55% year-over-year, lifting services ARR to 18% of total. This gives us an advantage over Palo Alto's Cortex XDR, especially in mid-market where we offer 20% lower TCO.

Third, driving global expansion and leveraging regional tailwinds. North America stays our core at 62% of revenue, but international markets are accelerating growth. EMEA posted 48% year-over-year revenue growth to $89 million in Q3, driven by NIS2 Directive compliance, with EUC-compliant modules surging 320% in adoption among DACH companies. We landed deals with two FTSE 100 insurers, featuring cyber insurance underwriting integrations via our risk scoring API that cut premiums by 15-20%. APAC jumped 62% year-over-year to $67 million, tapping PDPA and similar regulations; Japan and Singapore now make up 40% of regional bookings, including a $15 million ACV hyperscaler win with AWS for native cloud workload protection. LatAm grew 120% from a small base, eyeing Brazil's LGPD opportunities. International revenue reached 38% of total, heading toward 45% by FY25. We've localized NexusShield XDR for 12 languages and added 150 sales engineers in EMEA and APAC, shortening go-to-market timelines by 40%.

Fourth, strengthening ecosystem partnerships and our M&A pipeline. Our partner network is deeper than ever, with channels accounting for 52% of Q3 bookings, up from 45% last year. Co-sell deals with Microsoft through Azure Sentinel integrations and ServiceNow created $210 million in pipeline, while AWS Marketplace generated $45 million in Q3 consumption revenue, up 78% year-over-year. On M&A, we completed the $320 million acquisition of ThreatLynx in July, enhancing OT/IoT security for critical infrastructure and adding 15% to ICS/OT ARR, with cross-sell opportunities into 40% of our base per CISA's 2024 directives. Our pipeline features two tuck-ins for supply chain risk management, post-SolarWinds lessons.

Overall, these efforts have total ARR up 29% to $1.6 billion, dollar-based net expansion at 128%, and Rule of 55 at 68. With $750 million in cash, we're innovating ahead of the curve in a market where ransomware is up 37% year-over-year per our threat intelligence, aligning with Chainalysis and Sophos, and nation-state threats like Volt Typhoon intensify. Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Patel: Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we had a strong Q3. Revenue for the quarter was $265 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. This growth stemmed from robust performance across all product lines. Our gross margin was 81%, and operating expenses came in at $195 million. Net income for the quarter was $58 million, or $0.72 per diluted share.

Turning to market share trends, which highlight the power of our platform-led approach in a cybersecurity environment with rising threats and digital shifts. IDC forecasts the global cybersecurity market hitting $225 billion by 2027 at a 12.4% CAGR, fueled by ransomware, state-sponsored advanced persistent threats, and moves to zero-trust and SASE. We're steadily gaining share in key areas via our integrated NexusShield XDR platform, now safeguarding over 4,500 enterprise customers and handling 15 trillion threat signals daily through NexusAI.

By segment, per the latest Gartner Magic Quadrant for Endpoint Protection Platforms where we held Leader status for the third straight quarter, and IDC's Cloud Security Gateway Tracker: In endpoint detection and response, our stronghold, Q3 share rose from 13.2% to 15.8%, beating the segment's 1.1% average growth for a 2.6-point year-over-year gain, taking from legacy vendors like Symantec and McAfee who lost 1.5 points combined due to lagging cloud-native shifts. NexusShield EDR's 99.7% zero-day detection, via unsupervised ML adapting to polymorphic malware in under 200 milliseconds, leads AV-TEST benchmarks over CrowdStrike's Falcon.

In cloud workload protection and CASB, amid 45% year-over-year cloud misconfig spikes from Palo Alto's Unit 42, our CWPP share climbed from 9.1% to 11.4%, driven by AWS, Azure, Google Cloud integrations via serverless NexusGuard. This tops Zscaler's 10.2% CASB share as firms consolidate on our SSE framework. Cloud-native ACV averaged $1.2 million in Q3, up 28% year-over-year, with hyperscaler multi-year deals.

For network security and secure web gateways, we grabbed 2.1 share points to 14.3% globally, closing in on Fortinet's NGFW. Our AI threat intelligence from 500+ billion daily events cut false positives 40%, enabling MTTR under 5 minutes.

Regionally: North America, 55% of revenue, holds 24.7% enterprise EDR share, up from 22.1%, boosted by CMMC 2.0 federal wins and 35% growth in regulated verticals post-Change Healthcare. EMEA, 25%, grew to 17.9% from 14.3% via GDPR/NIS2, doubling DACH footprint with Deutsche Telekom OEM adding €150 million pipeline RPO. APAC, 15%, gained 4.2 points to 12.6% amid 60% ransomware rise per Verizon DBIR, with Japanese banks picking our zero-trust NWAN over Cisco SecureX and Australian firms ditching Check Point. LATAM/other, 5%, at 8.1% with 50% QoQ Brazil bookings via Ingram Micro.

These gains reflect $450 million R&D over 18 months, ThreatLynx acquisition for behavioral analytics, quantum-resistant encryption against harvest-now-decrypt-later, and channels at 65% net new ARR with 90% AWS Marketplace YoY surge. We anticipate 3-5 more share points in FY25 targeting $50 billion SASE via NexusShield One, cutting vendor sprawl 60% per ESG.

Next, the effectiveness of our go-to-market strategy has fueled these results. Our GTM blends direct and channel for EDR, SASE, and AI threat intel via Nexus Platform, with product-led growth for mid-market and land-and-expand for enterprises in a $188 billion market per Gartner, up 12% amid ransomware and regs like GDPR 2.0/SEC rules.

Key metrics: Q3 ARR up 48% YoY to $428 million, accelerating from Q2's 42%, with 32% new ACV growth to $112 million—record net new logos. Customers at 4,200, up 28%; large deals >$1M ACV at 41% of bookings. NRR at 118%, expansions 22% of ARR via ZTNA module at 65% EDR adoption.

Efficiency shines: CAC payback to 14 months from 17, CAC down 25% to $48K/customer, LTV:CAC at 4.8x vs. 3.5x target. Win rates 62% overall, 68% head-to-head with CrowdStrike/Zscaler/Palo Alto, thanks to AI behavioral analytics spotting 30% more zero-days.

Regionally: NA 62% ARR, 52% growth via AWS Marketplace $65M RPO (140% YoY), Azure doubles, ServiceNow 15% pipeline. EMEA 41% growth despite macro, channels 65% bookings (up from 52%), elite program to 450 resellers like Exclusive Networks/Arrow, 75% partner closure, EMEA roadshow $28M pipeline. APAC 68% to 18% ARR, localized teams, sovereign clouds, Nexus Shield POC 42% conversion vs. 35% global.

Boosters: inbound 450K site visitors (60% YoY) from AI risk content like "AI Shadow Boxing" webinars (25K regs, 18% SQL); PLG freemium Nexus Lite 1,200 SMBs, 22% upgrade; verticals healthcare 55% HIPAA, financials 49% quantum fears, Okta/Ping integrations. RPO $1.2B up 55% YoY, 85% multi-year; Q4 ARR 45-50% growth eyed, $50M channel/APAC investment, AI guardrails pilot.

Now, outlook for Q4 billings, a key subscription indicator. We guide $268 million to $278 million, 11-15% sequential from Q3's $242 million, 18-22% YoY, for FY24 ~$1.02 billion, 24% up. Driven by net new ACV, large deal >125% quota, NRR 118%.

Product drivers: NexusShield XDR >40% Q3 bookings, GA 5.0 with gen AI autonomous hunting/behavioral analytics neutralizing LockBit 4.0 for 30% Fortune 1000, sub-50ms latency edges CrowdStrike/SentinelOne. Cloud 35% billings (from 28%), CNAPP AWS EKS/Azure AKS 45% YoY post-Log4Shell/60% misconfigs per Gartner; Q4 50% YoY via SASE ZTNA/SWG/DLP vs. Zscaler.

Regions: Americas 62%, 13% seq via hyperscalers/CMMC; EMEA 24% 16% YoY despite GDPR delays, OT/IoT for ICS-CERT; APAC 14% 32% YoY sovereign clouds amid 70% ransomware per Sophos, NTT/Ingram channels. Pillars: AI R&D $85M quantum crypto; M&A $450M EdgeDefend OT for $15B ICS; GTM sales +20%, 75% win vs. Cortex XDR. RPO $2.8B +28% YoY, current +35%, 90%+ retention. Risks: 95-day sales cycles >$1M, 2-pt USD forex. $650M cash, no debt; sets up 2025 margin expansion to 28% adjusted non-GAAP operating.

We are confident that we are well-positioned to continue to drive growth and profitability in the years to come.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the question and answer session. First question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the market share gains in EDR and cloud, how sustainable are they given competitive intensity, especially post-CrowdStrike outage dynamics?

Jordan Patel: Thanks, Mike. Our share gains are durable, rooted in superior tech like 99.7% zero-day detection and 40% false positive cuts, as benchmarks show. The CrowdStrike incident actually highlighted legacy risks, driving inquiries up 25% to our cloud-native NexusShield. With R&D fueling innovations like quantum-resistant crypto and channels at 65% ARR, we see 25%+ organic growth persisting as point solutions fatigue sets in.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Rodriguez with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Rodriguez: Great results. Can you expand on international momentum, particularly APAC and any hurdles there?

Alex Rivera: Absolutely, Lisa. APAC's 62% growth reflects ransomware spikes and regs like PDPA. Wins with Japanese banks and Australian firms show our zero-trust NWAN pulling share from Cisco/Check Point. We've localized, certified sovereign clouds, and boosted sales engineers, cutting latency 40%. Challenges like talent shortages favor us; channels via NTT/Ingram will scale SMBs for 45% international mix by FY25.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel: Thanks. On XDR autonomous response, how does the NVIDIA integration impact margins, and what's the competitive moat?

Chris Lopez: Good question, Raj. The Cyber Fusion Center with NVIDIA GPUs enables real-time analytics neutralizing 4.2M payloads at 75% auto-remediation, with MTTD under 5 minutes at 92% true positives—18% ahead of Falcon per G2. Margins benefit from scale on 15T signals; TCO 20% below Cortex XDR. Moat is our NexusAI ML adapting unsupervised to novel threats, validated by MITRE, positioning us for MDR growth to 1,200+ clients.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Wong with Barclays.

Emily Wong: Solid guidance. Thoughts on elongated cycles and forex—any conservatism baked in?

Jordan Patel: Thanks, Emily. Yes, 95-day cycles for $1M+ deals and 2-point USD drag are factored, but large deal productivity >125% quota and RPO $2.8B up 28% with 35% current growth signal strength. $650M cash lets us invest aggressively in AI, M&A like EdgeDefend, and channels. Guidance assumes no major shocks; we're set for margin expansion.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, everyone, for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident that we can continue to deliver strong results.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.Market share trends: Gaining share in EDR (13.2% to 15.8%, +2.6 pts YoY), CWPP/CASB (9.1% to 11.4%), network security/SWG (to 14.3%, +2.1 pts); regionally NA EDR to 24.7%, EMEA to 17.9%, APAC to 12.6%; driven by platform integration, R&D, and acquisitions, targeting 3-5 more pts in FY25.
aspect_summary.Progress on key strategic initiatives: Accelerated zero trust/SASE (Zero Trust ARR +42% YoY to $456M, 28% of total); AI/ML XDR (upsells +150% YoY, RPO +31% to $2.1B); global expansion (intl rev 38%, EMEA +48%, APAC +62%, LatAm +120%); partnerships/M&A (channels 52% bookings, ThreatLynx acquired adding 15% to ICS/OT ARR).
aspect_summary.Next quarter billings guidance: Q4 billings $268-278M, +11-15% sequentially from Q3 $242M, +18-22% YoY; FY24 ~$1.02B +24% YoY.
aspect_summary.Effectiveness of go-to-market strategy: Strong metrics with Q3 ARR +48% YoY to $428M, NRR 118%, CAC payback 14 months (down from 17), win rates 62% overall/68% head-to-head; channels 52-65% bookings, PLG freemium upgrades 22%, inbound growth, regional strength (e.g., APAC +68%).
